questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ranking and location of UC Berkeley (The Bay Area is super nice).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything is sent to you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in an introduction week where everything practical was explained.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not too hard. However, it is costly, and there are a lot of scammers in the housing Facebook groups. 
I can recommend applying for International House.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be careful with scammers (always see the place or get it verified somehow). Furthermore, there are some areas that I would avoid living in (e.g., near Peoples Park and in the suburbs of Oakland).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online through CalCentral (the platform of UC Berkeley). You will receive several emails explaining when and how to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact student advisors or professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You have to be ready when your registration period begins. 
If you get waitlisted or do not get into classes, you want to take, try and contact the professor (they usually are willing to help you).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty easy compared to UCPH (note, however, that I only took undergraduate courses).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. The only differences are that you have midterm exams, and the professors engage more with the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* Econ C110: Game Theory in the social sciences
* EPS 198: Directed Group Study (Decal Course: Scuba and Ocean Conservation)
* Philos 128: Philosophy of Science
* POLSCI 179: Undergraduate Colloquium on Political Science (Fall 2022) 
* UGBA 104: Introduction to Business Analytics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
* UGBA 104: Introduction to Business Analytics. It is taken at Haas School of Business. It is pretty straightforward but gives an excellent intuition of how to use machine learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and linear optimization to solve real-world problems.
* POLSCI 179: Undergraduate Colloquium on Political Science. Easy and exciting 1 unit course (good course if you need one more unit)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of service/administration fees in the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is costly. The food was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. You can join every club imaginable (they have a list they will send you at the start of the semester).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in non-academic activities through UC Berkeley, so I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are soooo many things to see. I can recommend Yosemite, Las Vegas, Hawaii, San Diego, Santa Barbara, and Highway one.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone is very welcoming and outgoing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in in-class discussions. Join some clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Strangers will talk to you while taking public transportation. I had to get used to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are very outgoing and easy to connect with.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Apply for a lot of grants (it's going to get expensive)
- Travel a lot (there are so many exciting places in and near California)
- Don't spend too much time on school (the exams are pretty straightforward, and the most valuable experience is not academic).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty random, but; Do not buy a one-way plane ticket. Instead, buy a round-trip ticket (it is usually a lot cheaper).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the traveling and the new people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding enough time to travel.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
